MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron fires on the **first sub-word fragment of a rare, multi-token word** (e.g. " utens|il", " hippoc|ampus", " pracov|ních", " Tillerson", " DPR") and is strongly suppressed on the **trailing continuation pieces** of such words ("zzarella", "rgyz", "melon", "thane") — i.e. it encodes word-initial vs. word-final subword position rather than any semantic content.

This is a weak, largely noisy neuron whose top (positive) activations land on the opening token of formulaic identifier strings — the first digits of a year or ZIP code ("188"8-1890, "481"11), an initial like "T".B. Joshua, ordinal titles ("Second Year Council") — plus diffuse low firing across repeated marketing boilerplate, while it is strongly *suppressed* on highly predictable continuation tokens inside fixed strings (the "(" that opens an acronym expansion, "of" in "First of all", mid-tokens of part numbers/drug names).
